title: June 2026: thesis more validated — the head-fake phase is live
html:
Verdict: MORE validated. Every element of the fingerprint is present, and the damage is now migrating from the headline rate into participation — exactly the head-fake this tracker warns about.

Since the May turn: Hires rate stuck at 3.4% (cycle lows) and openings fell 7.59M → 7.36M (rate 4.6% → 4.4%), while layoffs held at 1.1% and initial claims sat near 2026 lows (~197K; 4-wk avg ~203K) — nobody is firing, nobody is hiring. Quits rate stayed low at 2.0%, though the level rose to 3.23M, a one-year high — a contrarian wrinkle worth watching. U-3 ticked down 4.3% → 4.2%, but entirely because participation fell 0.3pp to 61.5% (lowest since Mar 2021); prime-age EPOP dropped 0.6pp to 80.2%, the lowest since Dec 2022 (prime-age men −0.9pp to 85.7%). Long-term unemployed reached 1.9M — 27.3% of all unemployed, a four-year high — with mean duration at 25.5 weeks. Continuing claims (~1.78M) against initial (~197K) ≈ 9×: flat inflows, slow outflows — the newly unemployed can't get rehired.

Notable: the openings decline was concentrated in health care & social assistance (−147K) — the last reliable hiring engine cooling — plus leisure & hospitality (−86K) and wholesale trade (−74K); transportation/warehousing/utilities added +97K. Payrolls +57K in June confirm hiring, not firing, is the weak link. Falsification would require a claims/layoff spike; there is no sign of one.

Sources: BLS JOLTS (rel. Aug 4), BLS Employment Situation — June (rel. Jul 2), DOL weekly claims (rel. Jul 30). Next turn: July JOLTS, expected early September.
